samples.question: This page shows one black figure and several coloured decorations. Only the black ink and the green patch decide the answer; blue, orange, grey and purple marks are decoration and never count, even when they are drawn one inside another. Black ink is a solid wall that you cannot pass through. Exactly one small green patch is painted on the page. Imagine walking from the green patch to the edge of the page. You may walk freely over white space, over the green patch and over any decoration colour, and you may never step on black ink. Count how many separate black walls you must pass through on the way out, choosing the route that passes through as few walls as possible. A wall that has a visible gap cut through it does not have to be passed through at all, because you can walk out through that gap instead. How big the black figure is, where it sits on the page, how much black ink it holds, how many chambers it has, and how many nested outlines you can see anywhere on the page never decide the answer. How many separate black walls must you pass through to get from the green patch to the edge of the page? Answer 1 or 2.
